scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field manual-read route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target for the Aug-Sep 2026 period, covering 9,200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: Of disputed bills in the billing-db, 1240 are read_type ESTIMATED and 1785 are read_type ACTUAL.

F-03.statement: The billing-db tariff_change_log returned 0 records, indicating no tariff change occurred during the reviewed period.

F-04.statement: CRM dispute_response_times for the surge period show median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets.

F-05.statement: CRM dispute_volume_monthly shows 610 disputes in 2026-06, 590 in 2026-07, 1180 in 2026-08, and 1260 in 2026-09, i.e. roughly a doubling from Jul to Aug.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes but these are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle returned 320 account records (320 distinct account_id, 40 distinct route values), fields limited to account_id and route.

F-08.statement: route-log.lagging_routes returned 14 records with fields completion and route; completion and route each had 14 distinct values (sample: completion 0.7, route R-00).

F-09.statement: mdms-export.read_events_for_disputed_estimated returned 2 records for disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts: 1184 with ami_read_before_cutoff=true, billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, exported_to_billing=true; and 56 with ami_read_before_cutoff=false, billing_import_status=NO_READ_RECEIVED, exported_to_billing=false.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a customer-service response/triage capacity problem, so auto-answering tickets would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August is causing bills to be computed or accepted incorrectly, driving genuine billing errors and disputes.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: A degradation in the nightly AMI/MDMS read export (H-MDMS-BILL) since August is causing missing/invalid interval reads, forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: The contracted manual meter-read handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) started failing or under-delivering reads since August, increasing estimate substitution and bill errors.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Insufficient field-reading staffing is causing missed routes/reads, an upstream cause distinct from a one-off process failure, as SH-FIELD (biased toward staffing attribution and incentivized by headcount increase) might claim.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-OVERUS.statement: The 'estimate substitution when no accepted read' step itself became over-applied or miscalibrated since August, generating inaccurate bills independent of whether upstream reads actually failed.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR.statement: A billing computation, import-validation, or tariff error affecting bills with successfully recorded ACTUAL reads is driving the majority (1785 of 3025) of disputed bills, independent of any read-acquisition failure.

H-ROUTE-SPECIFIC-FACTORS.statement: The 14 lagging routes show widely varying completion rates (e.g. 0.70 for R-00) rather than a uniform shortfall, suggesting route-specific operational factors beyond a simple across-the-board staffing shortage may contribute to the route-completion gap measured in E-01.

H-AMI-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT.statement: A billing-import validation step rejects AMI reads flagged as high-consumption (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) even when the read was received and exported before cutoff, causing estimate substitution for 1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, independent of actual AMI delivery failure.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9,200 manual-read accounts, indicating a measurable shortfall in the contracted manual-read handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) during the dispute-surge window. This confirms a real route-completion gap but does not by itself identify the cause (staffing vs. other) or prove it produced billing errors/disputes.

Still shows a real route-completion gap: field manual-read completion was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026 across 9,200 manual-read accounts. It no longer supports PR-CHAIN-5's attribution of the ESTIMATED-read dispute pool to field manual-read shortfalls, since E-12 shows 95.5% (1184/1240) of that pool is AMI-channel reads rejected on billing import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), not field under-completion.

Of disputed bills, 1240 are on ESTIMATED reads and 1785 are on ACTUAL reads, so the majority of disputes (1785/3025 ≈ 59%) attach to bills built from a successfully recorded actual read, not an estimate substitution. This means causal chains routed through estimate substitution (AMI delivery failure, field read failure, estimate-substitution overuse) can at most explain the ESTIMATED-read disputes, leaving the larger ACTUAL-read dispute pool unexplained.

Still shows the disputed-bill split of 1240 ESTIMATED-read vs 1785 ACTUAL-read bills. It no longer supports treating the ESTIMATED-read pool as attributable to read-acquisition failure (field or AMI delivery) in general, since E-12 shows 95.5% of that pool arises from billing-import rejection of successfully delivered AMI reads (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), narrowing the mechanism to an import-validation defect rather than a read-failure chain.

The billing-db tariff_change_log shows 0 records, meaning no tariff change occurred during the reviewed period; this rules out tariff error as a cause within H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR but says nothing about billing computation or import-validation errors, which remain untested.

CRM dispute response times (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d) across 2440 tickets are within the 3.0-day SLA, indicating response/triage handling is not breaching its target during the surge. This further undermines the response-capacity framing of the dispute surge rather than confirming it.

CRM monthly dispute counts show ~600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 (610, 590) stepping up to ~1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026, a near-exact doubling coincident with the reported August onset. This confirms the magnitude and timing of the surge itself but does not identify which upstream process is causing it.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's unprompted claim that there has been no tariff change this year echoes, but does not add authority beyond, the already-authoritative E-03 (tariff_change_log, 0 records). As a stakeholder statement it is non-authoritative and does not independently resolve whether billing computation or import-validation errors (rather than tariff) explain the ACTUAL-read dispute majority.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative) claims a reader staffing shortfall of three positions since July causes manual-read routes to run late, producing estimated bills for those affected customers. This offers a candidate explanation for the route-completion shortfall already measured in E-01, but as a stakeholder claim it only speaks to the ESTIMATED-read dispute pool, not the larger ACTUAL-read majority that other hypotheses must still explain.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 confirms the utility may request field route priority changes but execution requires confirmation from the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD); this is an authority/governance document for the push_route_update protected action, not evidence about billing dispute causation.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle returned 320 accounts (all distinct account_id) that received estimated bills last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes, but the record only carries account_id and route — no read_type, tariff, or import-validation status fields. This means the query cannot by itself diagnose a billing computation/import-validation defect on the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed accounts (E-02) that W-WI-1 targeted; it instead gives a route-level account listing for the ESTIMATED population that could be joined with route-log lagging_routes data.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-10) identifies 14 specific routes behind schedule, each with a distinct completion value (sample: R-00 at 0.70), but the record carries only route and completion fields — no staffing, reader-assignment, or account linkage. This gives a concrete, heterogeneous breakdown of the route-completion shortfall already measured in aggregate by E-01, but by itself cannot attribute the lagging routes to staffing shortage versus another operational factor.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative, stakeholder) claims vendor ticket TX-4471 has provisioned MDMS export access for Lakeside as of today; this is a claim about access/precondition, not a data observation, and does not itself report any AMI read-event content relevant to the ESTIMATED-read dispute pool.

The 1184+56=1240 total exactly matches E-02's ESTIMATED-read dispute count, indicating billing-import rejection of valid high-consumption AMI reads — not AMI delivery failure — is the dominant mechanism (95.5%) forcing estimate substitution in this pool.
